findings.reason: Confirmed (high). On arXiv v3 p. 21 (§5.3, published p. 20), the paper says 'The spinor representation of SO10 corresponds to a rank 16 vector bundle S+ on the classifying stack BSO10'. It also states Mukai's equivalence (5.10) M°_7 ≅ [(Gr(7,S+)∖∆)/SO10], with Gr(7−n,Q_n) built over BSO10 in (5.13) and Lemma 5.13. Item /60 copies all of this. Both statements fail as written. The half-spin representation of Spin_10 is faithful on the centre μ_4, so −1 ∈ ker(Spin_10 → SO_10) acts by −Id on S+, and S+ is not an SO_10-representation. No rank-16 bundle S+ on BSO_10 exists. Moreover, −I_10 ∈ SO_10 lifts to a central element of order 4, which acts on S+ by a scalar, and so trivially on PS+, on OG(5,10) and on Gr(7,S+). Every point of the SO_10 quotient therefore has μ_2 in its stabilizer, and the quotient is a μ_2-gerbe over the quotient by the effective group PSO_10 (the image of Spin_10 in PGL(S+)). It is not M°_7. The paper's results are rational, and the repair keeps them. Over Q, A*(BSpin_10) ≅ A*(BSO_10), and a gerbe banded by a finite group induces isomorphisms on rational Chow groups and cohomology, so working with [U/Spin_10] (where S+ is genuine) or the rigidified quotient gives the same rational Chow ring and CKgP. The fix is right in asking for a recorded source error, a Spin or rigidified presentation with the comparisons proved, and checks on the central actions.

Confirmed (high). Item /13 states cl: A_i(X) → W_{2i}H^{2i}(X), 'compatible with proper pushforward'. The paper's Chow groups are graded by dimension. In the proof of Lemma 4.3 (v3 pp. 12–13), the diagonal lies in A_d(X × X) with d = dim X, and the lemma itself is stated for the ungraded sum ⊕_i A_i(X) → ⊕_k W_kH^k(X). With dimension grading, the class of a point in A_0(P²) would land in H^0 and not H^4, so the graded formula and its pushforward compatibility are false. The fix is right: either A^i → W_{2i}H^{2i}, or A_i → W_{2d−2i}H^{2d−2i} on pure d-dimensional X, with the P² tests.

Confirmed (high). Route 1's brief requires 'the moduli stacks M_{g,n} and M̄_{g,n} as smooth proper Deligne–Mumford stacks'. The open stack M_{g,n} is not proper: M_{0,4} ≅ P¹ ∖ {0,1,∞} is not proper. The paper's §4 exists to handle the non-proper M_{g,n} through Lemma 4.3 ('an open substack of a smooth proper Deligne–Mumford stack'), and item /2 states the distinction correctly. The fix is right.

Confirmed (medium), with two corrections to the red team's own bindings. I resolved the identifiers through the arXiv API: 1310.3859 is a Kelvin–Helmholtz SPH simulation paper, 1408.4509 a paper on GRB jets, and 2110.11061 'Polyadic Sets and Homomorphism Counting'. None is a source of the paper, while 2208.02357 is Canning–Larson's 'On the Chow and cohomology rings of moduli spaces of stable curves' (CLP [5]). Crossref gives the published article as Forum Math. Pi 12, e23, not e22. The Mukai DOI in prerequisite 10, 10.2307/2374777, does not resolve, while 10.2307/2375032 is 'Curves and Symmetric Spaces, I', Amer. J. Math. 117, 1627 (CLP [21]). CLP's reference list (v3) has [27] Petersen, Pacific J. Math. 275, [28] Petersen, Compositio 152, [3] Bergström–Faber, Épijournal 7, [2] the GitHub software and [34] Totaro, 'The motive of a classifying space', used for the CKgP equivalence on p. 20. Correction 1: Petersen–Tavakol–Yin is CLP [29], not [30]; [30] is Petersen–Tommasi, Invent. Math. 196 (2014), cited on pp. 3 and 8. Prerequisite 9 conflates the two, so both should be listed separately. Correction 2: Bergström–Faber arXiv:2207.05130 resolves to the Chenevier–Lannes paper, so it is [3], as the red team says. The rest of the fix is right.

Confirmed (medium). On v3 p. 29 (proof of Lemma 7.3, published p. 27) the paper prints 'the S12 action on the symbols Mij is Ind^{S12}_{S10}(V_{1^10}) = V_{2,1^10} ⊕ V_{3,1^9}, which is a sum of irreducible representations of dimension 11 and 55'. The left side has dimension [S_12 : S_10] = 132, and the right side 11 + 55 = 66. The symbols M_ij are indexed by unordered pairs, so the stabilizer is S_10 × S_2, and Ind_{S10×S2}^{S12}(sgn ⊠ 1) has dimension 66. By Pieri, adding a horizontal 2-strip to (1^10) gives exactly (3,1^9) and (2,1^10), of dimensions C(11,2) = 55 and C(11,1) = 11. The paper's argument (891 − 55 = 836) is unaffected. The fix is right.
